# QRG language reference

A QRG game is **JavaScript**: the body of a function that ends by returning a function that is called 60 times per second.
Everything below is available to the game without importing anything. The whole program has to fit in a QR code
(about 2.9 KB after compression), so it is meant to be short.

```js
let x = 120, y = 110, score = 0;          // your own variables

return i => {                             // runs every frame; `i` holds the input
  cls(NAVY);                              // library functions are just in scope
  if (i.l) x -= 2;                        // d-pad / arrow key / swipe left
  if (i.A) { score++; s(600); }           // A button / tap
  r(x, y, 16, 16, ORANGE);
  t('SCORE ' + score, 4, 4, WHITE);
};
```

## The screen

* 256 × 240 pixels, **16 colors** (the palette below), no anti-aliasing. Colors are numbers 0-15 or the names `BLACK` … `PEACH`.
* Text uses a built-in 3 × 5 pixel font; sprites are 8 × 8 pixels, one bit per pixel, drawn in any palette color.
* The game runs at a fixed 60 frames per second on every device.

## Rules of the language

* Your variables may have **any name**, even the name of a library function: `let r = 5` is fine (it only hides `r()` inside your game).
* A game must end with `return i => { ... }`. Errors are shown on the screen and sent to the editor.
* A game runs in a sandbox: it cannot use the network, cookies, the page, or other games' data. `save` / `load` are the only way to keep data.
* **Memory is private to the game.** `save` stores into a memory slot derived from a fingerprint of the game's code, so a game can keep
  things (a high score, a pet that is still alive tomorrow) without ever seeing another game's data. The ↺ button in the game view forgets it.
* Randomness: `R(n)`, `rand()` and friends use `Math.random` unless you call `seed(n)`.

## Input — the argument of the frame function

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `i.l  i.r  i.u  i.d` | D-pad, arrow keys or swipe: held down |
| `i.a  i.b  i.s` | A, B and Start buttons: held down (a tap on the screen counts as A) |
| `i.L  i.R  i.U  i.D` | Direction pressed this frame (repeats while held) |
| `i.A  i.B  i.S` | A, B, Start pressed this frame |
| `i.t` | Finger is touching the screen |
| `i.C` | Finger touched down this frame |
| `i.x  i.y` | Finger position in screen pixels (0-255, 0-239) |
| `i.T` | Frame counter (60 per second) |

Gestures are mapped onto these fields: a **swipe** becomes a direction press (and repeats while the finger keeps dragging),
a **tap** becomes `A`. The on-screen pad and the keyboard (arrows, Z / Space = A, X = B, Enter = Start) feed the same fields.

## Library

### Screen

**`W, H`** — Screen size in pixels: `W` = 256, `H` = 240.

**`cls(k = 0)`** — Fill the whole screen with color `k`.

```js
cls(NAVY)
```

**`r(x, y, w, h, k)`** — Filled rectangle of color `k` (0-15). Coordinates may be fractional.

```js
r(10, 10, 32, 16, RED)
```

**`box(x, y, w, h, k)`** — Rectangle outline, 1 pixel thick.

```js
box(0, 0, W, H, WHITE)
```

**`line(x1, y1, x2, y2, k)`** — One-pixel line.

```js
line(0, 0, 255, 239, YELLOW)
```

**`circ(x, y, radius, k)`** — Filled circle centered on (x, y).

```js
circ(128, 120, 20, PINK)
```

**`ring(x, y, radius, k)`** — Circle outline.

```js
ring(128, 120, 30, WHITE)
```

**`bar(x, y, w, h, value, max = 100, k)`** — Progress bar with a border. Green above half, yellow above a quarter, red below, unless a color `k` is given.

```js
bar(4, 4, 56, 7, hunger)
```

### Text

**`t(text, x, y, k, z = 1)`** — Draw text with the built-in 3x5 pixel font at integer scale `z`. Characters: A-Z (lower case is upper-cased), 0-9 and `: . - ! / + % ? , = > < ( ) * ' # _` and space.

```js
t('SCORE ' + score, 4, 4, WHITE)
```

**`tc(text, y, k, z = 1)`** — Same as `t`, horizontally centered on the screen.

```js
tc('GAME OVER', 100, RED, 2)
```

**`tw(text, z = 1)`** — Width of a text in pixels (each character is 4 pixels wide including spacing).

### Sprites

**`d(sprite, x, y, k, z = 1)`** — Draw an 8x8 one-bit sprite in color `k`, scaled by integer `z`. `sprite` is an array of 8 bytes (one per row, most significant bit = left pixel) or the name of a built-in sprite.

```js
d([60,126,255,255,126,102,102,0], 20, 20, WHITE, 2);  d('heart', 50, 20, RED, 2)
```

**`flip(sprite)`** — Returns a horizontally mirrored copy of a sprite.

```js
d(flip('rider'), x, y, WHITE, 2)
```

**`SP.name`** — Built-in sprite library (see list below), e.g. `SP.heart`, `SP.coin`, `SP.knight`.

```js
d(SP.star, 10, 10, YELLOW, 3)
```

### Colors

**`PAL[k]`** — The 16-color palette as CSS strings.

**`BLACK ... PEACH`** — Constants for the palette indexes 0-15, so you can write `RED` instead of `8`.

### Input helpers

**`tap(x, y, w, h)`** — True in the frame when the finger touched down inside the rectangle.

```js
if (tap(0, 0, 64, 64)) score++
```

**`over(x, y, w, h)`** — True while the finger is down inside the rectangle.

**`inb(px, py, x, y, w, h)`** — True when the point (px, py) is inside the rectangle.

**`btn(label, x, y, w, h, k = GRAY)`** — Draws a push button and returns true in the frame it is tapped.

```js
if (btn('START', 90, 100, 76, 24)) init()
```

### Random & math

**`R(n)`** — Random integer from 0 to n-1.

```js
x = R(W)
```

**`rr(a, b)`** — Random integer from a to b (both included).

**`rand()`** — Random number in [0, 1).

**`seed(n)`** — Makes all random functions repeatable: the same seed always gives the same sequence. Handy for shareable levels.

```js
seed(42); map = makeMap()
```

**`pick(array)`** — A random element of an array.

**`shuf(array)`** — A shuffled copy of an array.

**`clamp(v, min, max)`** — Limits `v` to the range [min, max].

**`lerp(a, b, t)`** — Linear interpolation: a when t = 0, b when t = 1.

**`dist(x1, y1, x2, y2)`** — Distance between two points.

**`sign(v)`** — -1, 0 or 1.

**`wrap(v, n)`** — Modulo that also works for negative numbers: `wrap(-1, 5)` is 4.

### Time

**`every(n)`** — True once every `n` frames (the game runs at 60 frames per second).

```js
if (every(60)) seconds++
```

**`now()`** — Wall-clock time in seconds (use it with `save`/`load` for things that continue while the game is closed).

### Actors

**`kind(sprite, k = WHITE, z = 1)`** — Defines a type of moving object: its sprite, color and scale.

```js
const coin = kind('coin', YELLOW, 2)
```

**`add(kind, x, y, props)`** — Creates an object (an "actor") with fields `x y vx vy w h c on k`. `props` overrides fields. Returns the actor.

```js
add(coin, R(W), 0, { vy: 2 })
```

**`all(kind)`** — Array of living actors of a kind (all kinds when omitted).

**`each(kind, fn)`** — Calls `fn(actor)` for every living actor of a kind.

```js
each(coin, a => a.vy += .1)
```

**`kill(actor)`** — Removes an actor (at the next `step`).

**`touch(kindA, kindB, fn)`** — Calls `fn(a, b)` for every pair that overlaps.

```js
touch(player, coin, (p, c) => { kill(c); score++ })
```

**`hit(a, b)`** — True when two objects with `x y w h` overlap.

**`step()`** — Moves every actor by its speed (`vx`, `vy`) and removes the dead ones. Call once per frame.

**`draw()`** — Draws every actor with its sprite. Call once per frame.

**`clear()`** — Removes all actors.

### Grids & paths

**`grid(cols, rows, fill = 0)`** — A flat array of `cols * rows` cells with the extra fields `.c` and `.r`.

```js
const map = grid(16, 11, 0)
```

**`gget(grid, x, y)`** — Value of a cell, or -1 outside the grid.

**`gset(grid, x, y, value)`** — Sets a cell (ignored outside the grid).

**`flood(cols, rows, sx, sy, max, cost)`** — Cheapest walking cost from (sx, sy) to every cell, as an array of `cols * rows` numbers (-1 = not reachable within `max`). `cost(x, y)` returns the price of entering a cell, or anything that is not a number to block it. 4-way movement.

```js
const D = flood(16, 11, ux, uy, 3, (x, y) => map[y*16+x] == 1 ? 2 : map[y*16+x] > 1 ? null : 1)
```

### Sound

**`s(hz, ms = 70, type = "square")`** — Plays a beep.

```js
s(880)
```

**`mel(notes, ms = 100, type)`** — Plays a melody: an array of frequencies, 0 = rest.

```js
mel([523, 659, 784, 1047], 120)
```

### Storage

**`save(key, value)`** — Writes a value (anything JSON can hold: numbers, text, lists, objects) to this game's private memory on this device. The memory belongs to the game alone: it is keyed by a fingerprint of the game's code (comments and spacing do not count), so no other game can read or change it, and a game whose code changed starts with an empty memory. About 1.5 KB per value, 32 keys. It lets a game go on while it is closed: save the time with `now()` and replay it on the next start (see the Tiny Pet demo).

```js
save('best', score)
```

**`load(key, default)`** — Reads a stored value (or `default` when nothing was saved).

```js
best = load('best', 0)
```

## Built-in sprites

Use them by name: `d('heart', x, y, RED, 2)` or `d(SP.heart, x, y, RED, 2)`.

```text
heart  star  coin  skull  sword  shield  tree  house  apple  fish  bone  ball  ring  gem  key  flag  up  plus  cross  check  smile  sad  sun  moon  cloud  drop  flame  mushroom  poop  zzz  meat  knight  archer  rider  rock  wave  block  right  down  left
```

A sprite is just 8 numbers, so you can make your own: each number is one row, the most significant bit is the left pixel.

```js
d([24, 60, 126, 255, 255, 126, 60, 24], 100, 100, YELLOW, 4);
```

## Limits

* About **2.9 KB** of compressed code (QR version 40). Typical games are 400–1500 bytes of code; the two large demos, *Tactics* and *Tiny Pet*, are 3–4 KB.
* Storage: 32 keys per game, about 1.5 KB per value.
* Sprites are 8 × 8, one color each; the screen has 16 fixed colors.
